title: Streamed call provenance telemetry and sanitizer orchestration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
We currently emit coarse-grained streaming telemetry that does not tie individual output chunks to provenance (which tool call produced it, which function invocation context, or the structured-output fragment). This creates three problems: (1) debugging tool/function call failures across progressive delivery is hard because logs/metrics are not correlated to streaming fragments, (2) redaction is inconsistent across partial outputs (sensitive tokens may be emitted and later redacted but traces and stored logs still leak), and (3) backward compatibility with legacy clients that expect event types for incremental outputs complicates instrumentation.

Goal:
Add a lightweight per-chunk provenance and span model plus a sanitizer orchestration layer that ensures logs/metrics exported from streaming paths are correlated, minimally invasive (low latency/CPU), and compatible with older incremental-event clients. Deliverables should include: chunk provenance IDs, deterministic span creation rules for tool calls and structured outputs, configurable sanitization policies with streaming-friendly algorithms, and a compatibility shim for legacy incremental events.

Proposed approach:
- Emit a short-lived chunk_prov_id on every progressive token/chunk event; the id is propagated to any downstream tool/function call and included in metric tags and trace spans.
- Create a lightweight tracing span per tool/function call that includes start/end markers and links to the originating chunk_prov_id(s). Spans should be coalesced when a single call services multiple chunks to limit overhead.
- Introduce a sanitizer orchestration component in the streaming path: a configurable pipeline of low-latency scrubbing steps (pattern redaction, PII classifiers, token-level allowlists) that runs inline before metrics/log export. The pipeline should be pluggable and support async fallback where latency SLOs are at risk.
- Add a compatibility layer that emits legacy incremental events (delta-chunk, delta-call-start/end) while preserving the new provenance id and span ids so observability consumers can adopt progressively.

Design and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Stream+Provenance+and+Sanitizer+Orchestration
- Draft telemetry schema: https://redwood.internal/docs/telemetry/stream-provenance-schema.md
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3412

Performance targets:
- Per-chunk provenance/trace tagging added overhead <= 0.5ms median per request on critical path (p95 < 2ms).
- Sanitizer pipeline tail latency contribution < 5ms median when using pattern-only rules; configurable async bypass for complex classifiers.
- Telemetry cardinality increase bounded: provenance id is ephemeral (TTL 1 minute) and not retained in high-cardinality long-term indices by default.

Observability outputs and dashboards:
- New dashboard: Stream Provenance Overview (per-model slice): chunk emit rate, per-chunk latency histogram, percent chunks with tool invocation, percent chunks redacted, per-span error rate.
- Traces: span tags = {chunk_prov_id, model, model_version, route, tool_name, call_status}.

Privacy and retention:
- Sanitizer pipeline must be applied before writing any chunk content to disk-based logs and before metric labels that could leak content. Only non-sensitive derived labels (e.g., has_tool_call=true) are stored long-term.

Rollout considerations:
- Feature-flag the provenance and sanitizer pipeline per-namespace so we can test on opt-in customers.
- Start with internal and low-volume customers, validate metrics/backfill, then enable broader rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- "Chunk provenance" id is present on every progressive event and is visible in the streaming API payload for new clients.
- Each tool/function call generates a trace span that links to the originating chunk_prov_id(s).
- Sanitizer pipeline runs in-path for pattern-based redaction and ensures no raw sensitive content is written to long-term logs or exported metrics labels.
- Compatibility shim emits legacy incremental event types with provenance ids preserved.
- Dashboards and trace queries surfaced in Console: Stream Provenance Overview and per-model span explorer.
- Performance regressions against the baseline are within targets above.
acceptance_criteria: Chunk provenance id emitted with each progressive chunk event and visible in streaming payloads
Tool/function call spans created and linkable back to chunk_prov_id
Sanitizer pipeline prevents raw sensitive content from being persisted in logs/metrics by default
Compatibility shim produces legacy incremental events while preserving provenance ids
Dashboards and trace queries available in Console for monitored namespaces
End-to-end latency and CPU overhead remain within specified performance targets
work_items: Spec: finalize telemetry schema and propagation rules (lead: Marcus)
Runtime: add chunk_prov_id generation + propagation hooks in streaming dispatcher
Runtime: span creation and coalescing logic for tool/function calls
Sanitizer: implement pattern-based inline scrubbing with plugin API
Compat shim: emit legacy incremental events with provenance tags
Console: dashboard and trace explorer updates
E2E tests: privacy assertions and perf benchmarks
Rollout: feature flag and staged enablement plan
risks_and_mitigation: Cardinality explosion if provenance ids are indexed long-term -> mitigation: ephemeral ids, strip from long-term indices, store aggregated counters only
Runtime overhead on tail latency -> mitigation: span coalescing, async sanitize fallback, feature-flag rollout
False negatives/positives in sanitizer -> mitigation: start with conservative pattern rules and opt-in ML classifiers; add monitoring for sanitizer errors
Compatibility regressions for legacy clients -> mitigation: compatibility shim and integration tests against old event parsers
qa_plan: Unit tests for chunk id propagation and span linking
Integration tests exercising tool calls across progressive delivery and asserting trace linkage
Privacy tests: ensure no raw chunk content in persisted logs/metrics for flagged namespaces
Perf tests: microbenchmarks for median and p95 impact on streaming path
Canary rollout to internal customers + monitor dashboards for anomalies
rollout_plan: Deploy feature-flagged runtime to staging and run synthetic streams (1 week)
Canary: enable for internal teams and 2 low-volume customers (2 weeks)
Wider opt-in to early customers and collect telemetry/feedback (3 weeks)
Default-on for low-risk namespaces after validation (target: runtime-1.20.2)
notes: Spoke with security: must run redaction before any metric labeling that contains text
Prototype PR shows acceptable perf on small models; larger seq-lengths need more testing
Need coordination with SDK teams for streaming payload schema bump
Consider adding TTL-GC for provenance ids in redis/memory stores
comments: 2025-02-11 - Marcus Rivera: Initial spike completed. Prototype generates chunk_prov_id and attaches to tool calls. Observed median overhead ~0.4ms on internal bench.
2025-02-13 - Sophie Patel (Design): UX note - Console should show provenance id as linkable to trace explorer; avoid exposing raw ids in public dashboards.
2025-02-15 - Security Team: Reviewed sanitizer approach. Approved pattern-based inline scrubbing; ML classifiers require separate sign-off.
2025-02-17 - QA: Added tests for sanitizer bypass mode and compat shim. Found an edge-case where coalescing dropped a span when a tool call spanned >60s; filed follow-up ENG-78300.
